newsitem.title: USA: J. Michaels shareholders approve merger.
newsitem.headline: J. Michaels shareholders approve merger.

text.p: J. Michaels Inc said on Thursday that the company's shareholders approved its merger with Muriel Siebert Capital Markets Group Inc, which owns the Muriel Siebert & Co discount brokerage and investment banking firm.
The company said shares of its stock would undergo a seven-for-one reverse stock split concurrently with the closing of the merger, expected on or before November 15.

After completion of the deal, existing shareholders will receive a cash payment from the sale of the assets and the right to share pro rata the remaining net after tax proceeds realized from the sale.
Shareholders of J. Michael will retain 2.5 percent of the stock of the surviving company, and shareholders of Siebert will own 97.5 percent of the shares.
The company will be renamed Siebert Financial Corp and will continue the existing brokerage business conducted by Muriel Siebert & Co, J. Michaels said.
Muriel Siebert, the chief executive of Siebert, will serve as the chief executive of the surviving company.
